title: Talk at WCCM-ECCOMAS 2026 (Munich)
content: Dr. Vivin Vinod will give a talk titled 'Active Learning and Multifidelity Machine Learning for Molecular Simulations' at the 17th World Congress on Computational Mechanics (WCCM) / 10th European Congress on Computational Methods in Applied Sciences and Engineering (ECCOMAS) in Munich. He will present active learning schemes, such as Low Fidelity as Bias (LFaB), alongside traditional multifidelity algorithms.

title: Preprint on an adaptive algorithm for MFML that reduces computational cost by up to 30 times!
content: Our most recent preprint 'Improvise, Adapt, Overcome: An On-The-Fly Multifidelity Algorithm for Efficient Machine Learning' has been hosted on arXiv. The work, co-authored with Peter Zaspel, develops and benchmarks a novel adaptive algorithm to determine the number of training samples at each fidelity in a multifidelity machine learning model enabling streamlining of data generation for quantum chemical machine learning.

title: Novel bias based Active Learning Scheme published in JCTC
content: Our paper 'LFaB: Low fidelity as Bias for Active Learning in the chemical configuration space' is now published with ACS JCTC. This work presents a novel bias-based active learning scheme utilizing affordable low-fidelity outputs. LFaB is shown to drastically reducing the number of training samples needed to achieve a certain model error.

title: Preprint on LC-DFT-level Excitation Energies for Light Harvesting Complexes
content: Our new preprint '∆-Machine Learning for LC-DFT-level Excitation Energies of Bacteriochlorophyll Molecules in a LH2 Complex' has been published on ChemRxiv. The work, co-authored with Sayan Maity, Peter Zaspel, and Ulrich Kleinekathöfer, introduces robust delta-ML models designed for high-fidelity excitation calculations in light-harvesting systems.

title: MFML enables fast simulations of Porphyrin Light-Harvesting Complexes
content: Our collaborative study, 'Excitation Energy Transfer between Porphyrin Dyes on a Clay Surface: A Study Employing Multifidelity Machine Learning', has been published in Advanced Theory and Simulations. It showcases how multifidelity machine learning models can scale the simulation of complex light-harvesting complexes on surfaces with extreme computational efficiency.

title: LFaB Active Learning Scheme Released on arXiv as a preprint
content: Our paper 'LFaB: Low fidelity as Bias for Active Learning in the chemical configuration space' is now available on arXiv. This paper presents a novel active learning scheme utilizing affordable low-fidelity representations to bias the active selection process, drastically reducing high-fidelity training data requirements.

title: Visiting Researcher to the Hausdorf Institute of Mathematics, Bonn
content: Dr. Vivin will join the Hausdorff Research Institute for Mathematics at the University of Bonn, as part of the DFG Flagship Winter School ‘Bridging multiscale, limited information, and low regularity in computational mathematics’. The Winter SChool is part of hte Junior Trimester Programe funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under Germany‘s Excellence Strategy – EXC-2047/2 – 390685813.

title: Dr. Vivin Vinod Begins Postdoctoral Assignment in Wuppertal
content: Dr. Vivin Vinod has officially started his postdoctoral research associate assignment at the University of Wuppertal. Continuing under the aegis of the Zaspel group, he will focus on kernel-based multifidelity method development and active learning strategies for molecular simulations.

title: PhDone: Vivin Vinod Defends with Summa Cum Laude!
content: Vivin Vinod successfully defended his Ph.D. dissertation titled 'Multifidelity machine learning methods for quantum chemical properties' at the University of Wuppertal. The examination committee (composed of Prof. Dr. Peter Zaspel, Prof. Dr. Ulrich Kleinekathöfer, Prof. Dr. Mario Barbatti, Prof. Dr. Matthias Bolten, and Prof. Dr. Matthias Ehrhardt) unanimously awarded Vivin his Dr. rer. nat. with the highest possible distinction: summa cum laude!

title: MFML enables fast and accurate predictions of CCSD(T) energies
content: Our collaborative paper, 'Predicting Molecular Energies of Small Organic Molecules With Multi‐Fidelity Methods', has been published in the Journal of Computational Chemistry. It explores the applications of GPR-based multi-fidelity techniques on predicting ground-state energies of structurally diverse organic molecules.

title: Talk at University of Potsdam (MESIGA25)
content: Presented 'Optimal Combination and Data Hierarchies in Multifidelity Machine Learning' at the MESIGA25 Seminar on Numerical Methods in Applied Mathematics. Spoke on the performance gains of o-MFML over standard single-fidelity structures for life-process chemical simulations.

title: Novel multifidelity method for predicting excitation energies reveals intricate fidelity hierarchy for ML-QC
content: Our paper, 'Investigating data hierarchies in multifidelity machine learning for excitation energies', is now available in the Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation. It analyzes the training data hierarchy and validates the high-efficiency Gamma-curve technique.

title: Benchmark study on data-cost efficiency places multifidelity methods at the epicenter of future research
content: Our benchmarking study, 'Benchmarking data efficiency in Δ-ML and multifidelity models for quantum chemistry', is officially available in JCP. The paper provides extensive performance insights on GPR accuracy trends under restricted sample sizes.

title: Work on assessing heterogenous multifidelity data Published in IOP:MLST
content: Our paper, 'Assessing non-nested configurations of multifidelity machine learning for quantum-chemical properties', has been published in Machine Learning: Science and Technology. It studies model predictions across unaligned multi-fidelity representations.

title: QeMFi Dataset Descriptor Paper Published in Nature Scientific Data
content: Our paper, 'QeMFi: A Multifidelity Dataset of Quantum Chemical Properties of Diverse Molecules', has been published in Nature's Scientific Data. QeMFi establishes a comprehensive open-source dataset explicitly engineered to benchmark high-accuracy, low-cost multifidelity algorithms in chemical configuration spaces.

title: QeMFi Dataset Published on Zenodo to help time-cost benchmarks in ML-QC
content: Our dataset, 'QeMFi: A Multifidelity Dataset of Quantum Chemical Properties of Diverse Molecules', has been published on Zenodo. QeMFi establishes a comprehensive TD-DFT dataset of five fidelities with properties such as excitation energies and transition dipole moments, to benchmark high-accuracy, low-cost multifidelity algorithms in chemical configuration spaces.

title: Seminar at SPP-2363 Annual Meet (Halle)
content: Presented a talk titled 'Optimized Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Quantum Chemistry' at the SPP-2363 Annual Meet, reviewing optimization bounds and dataset efficiencies.

title: Optimized MFML Method Published in MLST Journal
content: Our novel methodology paper, 'Optimized Multifidelity Machine Learning for Quantum Chemistry', has been published in Machine Learning: Science and Technology (IOP). This work presents the formulation of o-MFML as a robust successor to standard MFML frameworks.

title: Presented at Salzburg Young Chemists Summit
content: Gave a talk titled 'Optimized Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Quantum Chemistry' at Paris Lodron University in Salzburg, Austria, showcasing our methods to early-career researchers.

title: Relocation Completed: Joining Bergische Universität Wuppertal
content: The Zaspel research group has completed its relocation from Bremen to the Bergische Universität Wuppertal. Vivin Vinod has officially moved with the team to carry out his Ph.D. research in the new research space.

title: Excited State Energies Method Paper Published in JCTC
content: Our study, 'Multifidelity machine learning for molecular excitation energies', has been published in the Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation (ACS). It presents the core computational savings of combining TD-DFT and approximate methods.

title: Seminar at Fritz Haber Institute (Berlin)
content: Gave a detailed invited talk titled 'Optimized Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Quantum Chemical Properties' at the Theory Department of the Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society / Zuse Institute Berlin.

title: Talk at SIMPLAIX Workshop (Heidelberg)
content: Presented 'Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Excited State Energies' at the SIMPLAIX Workshop on Machine Learning for Multi-scale Molecular Modeling in Heidelberg.

title: Contributed Talk at SPP-2363 Meet (Halle)
content: Contributed a collaborative talk titled 'Multifidelity Machine Learning and Active Learning Strategies for Quantum Chemistry' during the SPP-2363 Annual Meeting.

title: Poster Presentation at MLQCDyn Workshop (France)
content: Presented a poster on 'Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Excited State Energies' at the MLQCDyn Workshop hosted by Université Gustave Eiffel in Champs-sur-Marne, France.

title: Vivin Vinod Joins the Zaspel Research Group as a Ph.D. Associate
content: Vivin Vinod has joined the research group of Prof. Dr. Peter Zaspel at Jacobs University, Bremen as a Ph.D. Research Associate. Coming from an interdisciplinary background in physics and economics, he will focus on kernel-based machine learning methods for complex quantum systems.

title: Talk on simviz Package at uRosConf 2021
content: Gave a collaborative talk at the International Conference on the Use of R in Official Statistics (uRosConf 2021) in Bucharest, Romania. Introduced the 'simviz' R package developed to simulate and visualize mobile telecommunication event data.

title: Voronoi Partition Talk at uRosConf 2021
content: Presented research titled 'Delauney Triangulation for Voronoi Partition for implementation in Simulated Mobile Network Data' during a session at the uRosConf 2021.

title: Policy Development Talk at University of Pisa
content: Delivered a policy development seminar titled 'Living conditions and Poverty in Italy - 2017. Small Area estimation and machine learning methods' organized by the Jean Monnet Chair EU.

title: Small Area Estimation Seminar at Scuola Sant'Anna (Pisa)
content: Delivered a seminar talk on 'Small area estimation methods for NUTS3 level poverty estimation in Italy' as part of the Small Area Estimation Seminar series in Pisa.

title: Research Talk at St. Stephen's College (Delhi)
content: Presented an experimental research talk titled 'Chua diode circuit as a secure communication device using chaos theory' at the prestigious Meera Memorial Paper Presentation at St. Stephen's College, University of Delhi, India.
